newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Monday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed today amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to easier but bond prices were narrowly mixed. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from last Friday's yield of 0.97/0.92 percent.
But one-year treasury bills ended at a yield of 1.57/1.52 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 1.60/1.55 percent.

Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.02/99.07 against last Friday's close of S$98.95/99.00, September 2001 at S$97.25/97.30 versus S$97.30/97.35 and June 2003 closed at S$95.25/95.30 from S$95.29/95.34.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from last Friday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
